terms.gloss: a case at law; one’s side in it
evidence: Cic. de Or. 2.199: causam agere (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: causam agere, to plead a case; causam dīcere, to defend oneself; causam obtinēre, to win it; causā cadere, to lose it (Lewis & Short). A civil case is a causa prīvāta, a criminal case a causa pūblica (Traupman 194).

evidence: Hor. Ars 78: adhūc sub jūdice līs est
terms.comment: Properly a quarrel, then a quarrel taken to court: lītem alicui intendere, to bring a lawsuit against someone (Cic. de Or. 1.42, Lewis & Short; Traupman 195).

phrases.latin: līs ad forum dēducta est, vespā jūdice
phrases.english: the case went to court, with a wasp as judge

phrases.latin: grammaticī certant et adhūc sub jūdice līs est
phrases.english: the scholars are at odds, and the case is still before the judge

phrases.latin: Estne causa prīvāta an causa pūblica?
phrases.english: Is it a civil case or a criminal case?

sources: Lewis & Short: causa · Lewis & Short: lis
